Q: Floor of Natural Logarithm A: 
import fractions

def floor_log(n):
    if n < 1:
        raise ValueError
    if n <= 2:
        return 0
    # find k such that:
    # k < ln(n) < k+1
    # e^k < n < e^(k+1)
    # 1/e^k > 1/n > 1/e^(k+1)
    # (e^-1)^k > 1/n > (e^-1)^(k+1)
    # n * (e^-1)^k > 1 > n * (e^-1)^(k+1)
    L = 0
    i = 1
    denominator = 1
    f = fractions.Fraction
    while True:
        # find successive upper and lower bounds, L_i < e^-1 < U_i,
        # until L_i^k > 1/n > U_i^(k+1) for some k.
        # That is, n * L_i^k > 1 > n * U_i^(k+1).
        # Then we will have
        # n * (e^-1)^k > n * L_i^k > 1 > n * U_i^(k+1) > n * (e^-1)^(k+1),
        # so n * (e^-1)^k > 1 > n * (e^-1)^(k+1)
        # as desired.
        #
        # Recall: e^-1 = 1 - 1 + 1/2! - 1/3! + 1/4! - ...
        # And, due to explicit bounds in Alternating Series Test:
        # Partial sum ending in a positive term will be an UPPER BOUND;
        # partial sum ending in a negative term will be a LOWER BOUND
        # for e^-1.
        i += 1
        denominator *= i
        U = L + f(1, denominator) # first value U = 1-1 + 1/2! = 1/2
        i += 1
        denominator *= i
        L = U - f(1, denominator) # first value L = 1-1 + 1/2! - 1/3! = 1/3
        k = 1
        lhs = n * L
        rhs = n * U*U
        assert lhs > rhs
        # If not then L*(L^(k-1)) < U*U*(L^(k-1)) < U*U*(U^(k-1)) for all k.
        # But it is true at L=1/4, U=1/3, so should always be true as
        # L gets larger and U gets smaller.
        # Now find k...
        k = 1
        while lhs > rhs:
            if lhs > 1 > rhs:
                return k
            if lhs < 1: # have gone too far, lhs will now be < 1 forever
                break # stop and get new L, U
            k += 1
            lhs *= L
            rhs *= U

for n in [2, 3, 26489122129, 26489122130, 4311231547115195, 4311231547115196, 11892590228282008819681954096389267309259354644229, 11892590228282008819681954096389267309259354644230]:
    result = floor_log(n)
    print(f'floor(ln({n})) = {result}')

Q: Different results between CLI and pre-commit A:

Pre-commit runs only on the files in the git repo.

So if a.py was not added to git, then it's only checked by ruff check and not pre-commit.

You can test this by (e.g.) git add a.py, then re-try pre-commit run --all

Q: Is the client certificate configured on an APIM Backend entity ever used at runtime? A:

Certificate added under credentials in backend settings is expected to be attached to request and presented to backend by APIM if backend requests it. It's mutual TLS.

Q: ggplot2 sample size annotation: How do you place the sample size under the x-axis? A:

If you do not need to do the labelling automatically. You can set the labels for the x scale to "MICRO\nn=32" and similar, where \n is new line.

Automating this is also possible. Below I provide an answer using data included in 'ggplot2' and not using additional packages. The solution I have come up with makes it necessary to provide the name of the data mpg a second time within the call to scale_x_discrete(). In scales, the argument to parameter labels can be a function, in which case it is passed as argument the existing group label. The anonymous function defined in-line adds the counts to these group labels, also inserting \n. Using sort() and rle() is one possible approach to obtaining the counts. This is (hopefully) a robust approach, that provides a correct plot irrespective of the ordering of factor levels, and or groups.

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mpg, aes(factor(cyl), hwy)) +
  stat_summary(geom = "col", fun = mean) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = 
                     function(x) {counts.rle <- rle(sort(mpg[["cyl"]]))
                                  counts.vec <- counts.rle[["lengths"]]
                                  names(counts.vec) <- counts.rle[["values"]]
                                  paste(x, counts.vec[x], sep = "\nn=")}
  )

In general, please, use easily available data or provide the data. Also indicate the packages used by including the library() call in the code.

Q: Google Spreadsheet: Skip empty queries when stacking multiple queries in one sheet A:

1 to 1 parity with your desired output:

=LET(da, Data!A2:O, 
     he, HSTACK("Date","City","Country","Attending","Duration"),
     re, VSTACK("Africa","Asia","Central America","Europe",
                "Middle East","North America","Oceania","South America"),
     st, "select A,B,C,E,F where D = '", tr, "' order by D,C", 
     ar, REDUCE(he, re, LAMBDA(x, y, LET(z, QUERY(da, st&y&tr, ), 
         VSTACK(x, IF(IFNA(z)="",,VSTACK(HSTACK(y, 
         WRAPROWS(,COLUMNS(he)-1,) ), z)))))), 
 FILTER(ar, INDEX(ar,,1)<>""))

#remove hydrogens from pep and drug

#combine mol and pep in same object

ADDENDUM

https://www.rdkit.org/docs/GettingStartedInPython.html#chem-vs-allchem

I searched more and found out that:

rdkit.Chem.AllChem.EmbedMolecule is equivalent to rdkit.Chem.rdDistGeom.EmbedMolecule; Chem vs AllChem

and the function is nicely explained at rdkit.Chem.rdDistGeom.EmbedMolecule where randomseed defaults to -1 and as in argument explanation.

randomSeedprovide a seed for the random number generator

so that the same coordinates can be obtained for a molecule on multiple runs. If -1, the RNG will not be seeded.

but there is more here:

EmbedMolecule() is no longer random?

So I get different conformers because each time I re-run my script default randomseed = -1 the RNG (random number generator) will not be seeded.

If I change :

AllChem.EmbedMolecule(drug, useRandomCoords=True) #works
AllChem.EmbedMolecule(pep, useRandomCoords=True)    #works

to

AllChem.EmbedMolecule(drug,randomSeed=1234,  useRandomCoords=True) #works
AllChem.EmbedMolecule(pep,,randomSeed=1234, useRandomCoords=True)    #works

I will end up with the same conformer/result.

Now I'll have to investigate useRandomCoords=True and check why using useRandomCoords=False fails, but only for the peptid (pep) or conjugate and not the drug.
